evidence:
Dictionary: 1-cos(2 pi j delta/p) summed with weights y_j is half the Laplacian eigenvalue at character delta of the weighted Cayley graph Cay(Z_p, {+-j}, y_j). So Gamma_s(p) is half the largest spectral gap under an l_{1/s} budget on the generator weights. With equal shares on K frequencies, the coverage equals K^{1-s} times the normalised gap of a 2K-regular abelian Cayley graph.

Sources (all PDFs fetched and read):
(1) Alon and Roichman, Random Cayley graphs and expanders, RSA 5(2):271-284, 1994.
- Thm 1: c(delta) log n random generators give an expander.
- Thm 2: (1+eps) log2 n random elements suffice for any abelian group; for Z_n, eps log2 n suffice.
- Prop 3 (Sec 3.1): "If A is an Abelian group of order n, and X(A,S) is a delta-expander, then |S| >= c log2 n."
- Abstract: "For Abelian groups this is essentially tight."
- Prop 7' uses a closed-walk (trace) count.
(2) Friedman, Murty and Tillich, Spectral estimates for Abelian Cayley graphs, JCTB 96(1):111-121, 2006.
- Abstract: "for fixed d, a d-regular Cayley graph on an Abelian group of order n has second eigenvalue bounded below by d - O(d n^{-4/d}) ... for a large odd prime n, the O(dn^{-4/d}) cannot be improved."
- With d=2K this is a normalised gap of at most C p^{-2/K}. That is the unweighted analogue of our Cor few / eq. (Kbound), which gives the weaker exponent p^{-1/(2 a_s K)} but holds for arbitrary weights.
- They mention a "large trace" approach, which is what our Bessel positive-Fourier inequality is.
(3) Cioaba, CRAS 342 (2006) 635-638: closed-walk lower bounds for abelian Cayley graphs. This is the combinatorial twin of our "resonances only add non-negative terms".
(4) McCracken et al., arXiv 2505.18266, Sec 4.3. Thm 4.7 and Cor 4.8: "Learning O(log n) distinct frequencies gives a logit margin Omega(log n)". The margin is unnormalised and only sufficiency is shown; they write "we don't know why it occurs"; no necessity bound; no expander citations.

Consequence: the equal-share restriction of thm:scaling (Theta((log p)^{1-s}), K = Theta(log p)) is essentially a corollary of AR Thm 2 plus FMT. Not found anywhere:
- the weighted two-sided bound under the concave l_{1/s} budget with explicit constants, for arbitrary weights;
- the maximiser support Theta(log p) and the share floor;
- the network statement gamma*_b = Theta(p^{-nu/2}(log p)^{1-nu/b}) over all product networks, and Cor few.

Checked and only related:
- Chowla cosine problem (Bourgain/Ruzsa/Sanders; Bedert arXiv 2509.05260; arXiv 2509.03490, 2609.05338). It concerns the negative tail of the cosine sum; ours is the near-period/Dirichlet tail.
- Small-bias sets (two-sided bias).
- Weighted Cayley sparsification (arXiv 2508.08078).

The paper already cites alon1994random, but only for the random lower bound; that bib entry is correct (Princeton record: RSA 5(2) 271-284, doi 10.1002/rsa.3240050203). The mccracken2025 bib entry is wrong: the correct first author is Gavin McCracken. Queries run: FMT second eigenvalue abelian; Alon-Roichman abelian log generators; weighted Cayley spectral gap log n; small-bias Z_p; Chowla cosine. Notes and PDFs: /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/r25-log-scaling/CHECK.md and src/.

recommended_citations.why: Supports the upper bound and Cor few in the equal-weight case. A d-regular abelian Cayley graph has lambda_2 >= d - O(d n^{-4/d}), tight at odd primes. With K frequencies (d=2K) the normalised coverage is O(p^{-2/K}), so o(log p) generators give a vanishing gap.

Already in refs.bib, but it should be cited for both directions. Thm 2 (with the Z_n remark after it) gives sufficiency of Theta(log p) random generators, which is our lower bound. Prop 3 shows that an abelian delta-expander needs |S| >= c log2 n, which is the unweighted form of the Theta(log p) support claim.

Thm 4.7 / Cor 4.8 (Sec 4.3): O(log n) random frequencies give an Omega(log n) unnormalised logit margin. This is prior ML art for the sufficiency half, which is our lower bound on Gamma_s. They state they do not know why log n occurs. The existing bib entry (Andrew McCracken) is wrong and should be replaced.
Optional. Lower-bounds closed walks in abelian Cayley graphs by counting balanced words. This is the combinatorial analogue of our positive-Fourier (heat-trace) inequality eq:posfourier.

recommended_change: In cyclic.tex after thm:scaling, or at the start of app:scaling, add: "Equivalently, sum_j y_j(1-cos(2 pi j delta/p)) is half the Laplacian eigenvalue at character delta of the weighted Cayley graph Cay(Z_p,{+-j}) with weights y_j. So Gamma_s(p) is the largest spectral gap of such a graph under an l_{1/s} budget on generator weights. For unweighted generator sets, Theta(log p) generators are known to be sufficient \citep[Thm. 2]{alon1994random} and necessary \citep[Prop. 3]{alon1994random}, and K generators leave a normalised gap O(p^{-2/K}) \citep{friedman2006spectral}. Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling} extends this to arbitrary weights under the concave budget, locates the maximiser and bounds its shares; the network consequence is new. \citet{mccracken2025} observed that O(log n) random frequencies give an Omega(log n) unnormalised logit margin; our upper bound shows this order is also necessary." In the appendix, next to eq:posfourier, optionally note that it is a heat-trace / closed-walk bound in the spirit of \citet{friedman2006spectral,cioaba2006closed}. Fix the mccracken2025 bib entry (Gavin McCracken et al., correct title). Keep the existing Alon-Roichman sentence. Do not describe the equal-share case as new: it follows from AR plus FMT.
